back: A way of writing expressions with each operator after its operands; needs no brackets or precedence rules.
Read left to right: push numbers; for an operator pop two values, apply it (first popped is the right operand) and push the result.
Operands go to the output; an operator pops higher or equal precedence operators from the stack first; ( is pushed; ) pops to (; empty the stack at the end.
Push operands as strings; for an operator pop two strings and push (left operator right).
No brackets or precedence at evaluation time; one left-to-right pass with a stack; easy for compilers and calculators.
Postfix 10 4 - means 10 - 4: the value popped first is the right-hand operand.
Operators of equal precedence are applied left to right, so 20 / 4 / 5 becomes 20 4 / 5 /.
